content: A jade stone cannot be polished without friction, nor a person perfected without trials.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Yu bu zhuo, bu cheng qi (玉不琢，不成器) — Book of Rites (Liji)
explanation: Raw jade pulled from the mountain riverbed looks like an ordinary, rough pebble. Only through grinding against abrasive sand and diamond dust does its luminous, translucent luster emerge. Trials, conflicts, and hardships are not life's mistakes; they are the grinding wheel that reveals your soul.
practicalInsight: When facing friction or opposition at work or in relationships today, welcome it as the abrasive powder polishing your character.
reflectionPrompt: What difficult circumstance are you currently resisting that is actually trying to polish your character?
